panels.title: Router cache locality
panels.description: The router's own view of prefix reuse, as two ratios that must be read apart. selected/query is what the chosen worker holds — the router's prediction of the engine's hit rate, and the only one comparable to the engine's sglang:cached_tokens_total / sglang:prompt_tokens_total. matched/query is the deepest prefix ANY worker in the fleet holds, so it reads structurally high: it counts selections that then routed elsewhere. The gap between the two lines is locality the routing decision gave up; the gap between selected/query and the engine's number is cache state that changed between selection and prefill. selected/query sitting BELOW the engine's rate is the third case and means a worker serves traffic while publishing no KV events — a failed /server_info probe or a page-size disagreement — not eviction. Kept per model_id: ratios are not additive across models.

panels.title: Cache-aware decisions
panels.description: Terminal outcome of every cache-aware selection. Evaluations, not requests — which is why the unit is not ops and the series are not stacked. cache_hit = a prefix owner won. no_candidates = the lookup ran and produced no usable owner (a cache problem). candidates_exhausted = owners existed and admission or the pressure guard rejected every one (a sizing problem). lookup_unavailable = no lookup happened at all — no routing tokens, no fleet block size established yet, or no provider configured; a router that has just started sits here until the first worker reports its page size. Selections that ended in a 503 are absent, in sgl_router_policy_selection_failures_total instead. Rates are additive across models, so model_id is collapsed here.

panels.title: Locality by decision
panels.description: selected/query split by the decision that produced it — which bucket is losing the locality. A low ratio under candidates_exhausted is capacity pushing requests off their prefix and is fixed by sizing, not by the cache. A low ratio under cache_hit means the winner held little to begin with: read it with Router cache locality, where a matched/query that is also low says the fleet simply does not hold this traffic's prefixes. no_candidates reads at or near 0 by construction. Kept per model_id: ratios are not additive across models.

targets.expr: sum by (model_id, decision) (rate(sgl_router_selected_overlap_blocks_total{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (model_id, decision) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_query_blocks_total{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Zero-match attribution
panels.description: Selections that matched nothing, split by whether the request's FIRST queried block hash exists anywhere in the tree. absent = no node carries it: the engines never published the block or already removed it, so the work is engine-side. in_tree = the hash IS carried but the root-anchored walk could not reach it, so the work is router-side linkage. A zero match is the most common outcome on an unhealthy fleet and these two faults live in different repositories; matched = 0 alone cannot tell them apart. Emitted only where the in-process tree is the provider — an external Indexer cannot answer this, and the panel is empty there rather than wrong.

panels.title: Lookup availability — fleet vs worst replica
panels.description: Share of cache-aware selections that got a prefix lookup at all (1 - lookup_unavailable). Every router replica maintains its own tree and its own block-size oracle, so one replica can lose the lookup while the fleet aggregate stays healthy — the worst-replica line is the only place that shows. A single replica at 0 while the fleet sits near 1 means that pod never learned the fleet's page size or lost its KV subscription, and everything it routes is going out blind. Both lines dropping together is a fleet-wide event: a rollout that changed the page size, or every subscription failing at once. Both expressions supply an explicit zero for an empty numerator: no lookup_unavailable samples at all is the healthy case, and 1 - <empty> is empty rather than 1, which would blank the panel precisely when nothing is wrong.

targets.expr: min(1 - ((sum without (decision) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{model_id=~"$model_id",decision="lookup_unavailable"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum without (decision) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0) / clamp_min(sum without (decision) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)))

panels.title: KV event blocks by medium
panels.description: Blocks/s the router tree consumes, by event kind and the storage-medium tag the engine put on the event, per deployment. On a hierarchical-cache fleet block_stored/CPU_PINNED runs at roughly the block_removed/GPU rate; they are not equal, because the engine also evicts device blocks it never backed up. A CPU_PINNED line at 0 while the engines report hicache backups means the tier stream is not reaching the router. Both the busiest and the quietest replica are plotted: every replica receives the full stream, so a quietest-replica line at 0 while the busiest is healthy means one replica has lost its subscription and is routing blind.

panels.title: KV tree blocks by tier (fleet)
panels.description: Blocks the router tree attributes to the fleet, by the tier the worker holds them on (a block held on device and host counts under both). Absolute counts, so summing across workers is valid. host should sit at roughly hicache-ratio times device on a fleet with a full host tier; host at 0 means routing cannot see the L2 tier at all. max per worker across replicas, then summed.

panels.title: Tree coverage of engine host tier
panels.description: Router-attributed host-tier tokens / engine hicache host tokens in use, per deployment. ~1: every block the engines hold on host is routable. ~0 with a full host tier: the L2 tier is invisible to routing and repeats of anything evicted from device land on random pods -- this is the ratio that separates a retention problem (the engines really evicted it) from a visibility problem (the engines still hold it, the router forgot). Above 1: the tree holds tiers a worker already released, so check sgl_router_kv_event_batches_lost_total -- a tagged removal clears only its own tier, and a batch lost in transit strands the rest. Both sides are grouped by namespace because the ratio is not additive across deployments.

targets.expr: (sum by (namespace) (max by (namespace, worker_url, dp_rank) (sgl_router_kv_tree_blocks{tier="host"})) * on(namespace) group_left() max by (namespace) (sgl_router_kv_block_size)) / sum by (namespace) (sglang_hicache_host_used_tokens{tp_rank="0"})

panels.title: Cache hits by tier served from
panels.description: Which storage tier the CHOSEN worker holds the matched prefix on, in the same vocabulary as KV tree blocks by tier: device = served in place, host = served by a load-back from host memory, disk / external = fetched from a storage backend. Two labels are not tiers. none = the chosen worker holds no part of this prefix, which is every no_candidates selection plus any hit whose winner was not the owner. unknown = the deployment routes through the out-of-process Indexer, whose wire contract carries no medium — the tier is not observable there, and this reports so rather than defaulting to device.

panels.title: Affinity routes served by load-back
panels.description: host / (device + host): the fraction of in-place-or-load-back hits that ride the host tier rather than device HBM. This is what the storage-tier work buys, stated as a number — before the tree honoured tiers, every one of these was a cold prefill on a random worker instead. Rising is normal as device turns over (the device tier holds minutes, host holds hours); rising toward 1 while the engines report a healthy device pool means device ownership is being revoked faster than it should be. Kept per model_id: ratios are not additive across models.
